artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan (3 waves, 1.5h) loosening the plan-checklist mark-completed instruction in the core, lean, and nix implementation agents off the literal '**Task {P}.{N}**:' prefix, with the canonical verbatim-quotable contract wording designated in general-implementation-agent.md Stage 4B-ii for the two downstream sibling tasks.

memory_candidates.content: Silent-failure pattern in agent instruction contracts: when an agent is told to Edit-match a literal template line shape (e.g. '- [ ] **Task {P}.{N}**: {description}') against an artifact produced by a DIFFERENT agent whose emission template is free-form, the match finds nothing and the agent proceeds without error. Observed live as 0 of 87 plan-checklist items ticked across 4 completed phases, which in turn zeroed a downstream drift metric that counted '- [x]' occurrences, making completed work read as 'no work done'. Two structural lessons: (1) a cross-agent instruction must describe what to LOCATE AND PRESERVE ('the item's existing text, whatever form it takes', tolerating formatting drift) rather than a template to match, because a producer-side template and a consumer-side match template drift independently and nothing detects the drift; (2) when the same idiom is copied across N agent files, designate one named canonical home (file plus section heading) that siblings quote verbatim, since N independent paraphrases reproduce exactly the inconsistency being fixed. Useful diagnostic signal: if a file already contains BOTH a brittle template-match phrasing and a loose text-agnostic phrasing of the same instruction, the loose one is usually the correct idiom and the brittle sites should be made consistent with it rather than new wording invented.
